The final list item after 'Vocalic Length' (HTML line 249) reads exactly: 'Accent. In any event, accent is predictable only from word or morphological boundaries. It is indicated only where it is unpredictable in the morphophonemic transcription used here.' -- verbatim match to the reported quote at the stated locator. The phoneme table on the same page lists 'Pitch / Accent ʹ', consistent with accent =…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word accent (realized as raised pitch) is non-contrastive and falls on the final syllable of the word; certain (inflectional/enclitic) suffixes do not take the accent, which then stays on the stem-final syllable -- i.e. final syllable of the stem/word, predictable from morphological boundaries. Corroborated by Strand 2007/2016 (same site, Nuristani-wide page): 'In the remaining languages [i.e. other than Kâmkata-vari and Vâsi-vari, hence including Kalaṣa-alâ] accent falls automatically on a word's final syllable (excluding inflectional or enclitic suffixes) and is not written', and second-hand by Halfmann 2024: 107-108 fn.66 citing Degener 1998: 36 (strictly fixed, phonemically non-distinctive stem-/word-final stress in Nuristani Kalasha).
new_statements.exceptions: 'forms with certain suffixes retain accent on the stem rather than the suffix' (Strand 2011); Strand 2007/2016 specifies the excluded suffixes as inflectional or enclitic, and notes that multi-word loan names joined by '+' are treated as one unit for final-syllable accent. Accent is written in Strand's transcription only where unpredictable, implying a residue of lexically marked items.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the word (stem plus derivational material), with inflectional/enclitic suffixes outside the accent domain; accent is phonetically a pitch rise (Strand 2007 'Accent' paragraph) and interacts with utterance-final intonation contours. Statement is for the Nišeigrâm (nišei-alâ) dialect; Strand 2007 generalizes it to Kalaṣa-alâ as a whole.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement describes Nišei-alâ, the dialect of Nišeigrâm (Nisheygram) village in the lower Waigal valley -- the same variety as Degener 1998 and the 'lower dialect' on which Grjunberg 1999 is based (Glottolog lists Nishey-ala / Chima-Nishey as a dialect under waig1243; no separate dialect glottocode verified here). Strand 2007/2016 extends the same automatic final-syllable accent to Kalaṣa-alâ as a whole (and Ashkun), contrasting it with distinctive accent position in Kâmkata-vari and Vâsi-vari; he separately notes phonemic vowel length in the Varǰan (upper, väi-alâ) dialects but no accentual difference.

The Iranica article, had it opened, would cover all Nuristani languages, not this dialect alone. The 'accent on the second rather than the last syllable' remark on Strand's Kalaṣa-of-Kalaṣüm page concerns the pronunciation of the ethnonym kalaṣa in the Indo-Aryan Kalasha of Chitral, not this language.

new_statements.relation_note: Same author, same placement and type as the catalog record (Strand 2011 Nišei-alâ sound system: accent usually final, some suffixed forms keep it on the stem, predictable from word/morphological boundaries) and nearly the same wording as the Strand 2007/2016 transcription page already held by the project ('accent falls automatically on a word's final syllable (excluding inflectional or enclitic suffixes)'); consistent with Halfmann 2024 fn. 66 (Nuristani Kalasha has fixed, phonemically nondistinctive stress, citing Degener 1998: 36). Adds nothing beyond the stem-final formulation; no contradiction.
new_statements.rule_in_words: In Kalaṣa-alâ (Kal., including the Nišei-alâ dialect Kal.n.), as in Âṣkuṇu and probably Tregâmi, accent position is not phonemic: it falls automatically on the last syllable of the word's stem (i.e. stem-final, inflectional endings not counted). Only Kâmkata-vari (K.) and Vâsi-vari (V.) have phonemic (lexically distinctive) accent position, and only there does Strand write the accent mark.
new_statements.exceptions: Domain is the stem, not the whole word (suffixes outside the stem do not take the accent); hedged with 'apparently' and a question mark for Tregâmi. Elsewhere the article mentions accent only as a conditioning factor in historical vowel changes ('In Kal., K.km., and V. further dorsal raising and fronting pushed accented u forward to ü'; 'In A., Kal., and K. accented a is rounded, except when it was in an ancient suffix').
new_statements.identity_note: The article treats all five Nuristani languages; the accent sentence covers Kalaṣa-alâ ('Waigali', abbr. Kal.) as a whole, whose dialects it lists as Varǰan (chief subdialect Vä-alâ, Kal.v.) and Čima-Nišei (chief Nišei-alâ of Nišeigrâm, Kal.n.); the catalog record is for Nišei-alâ specifically (Strand 2011).
